searchText: Well... "We" as in "me" focus on mainnet, nothing else. Anyway, even if we're not going ahead with eof this time around, I think we made great progress during the last two weeks. Thanks and congrats for this, I had a lot of fun <@403707149043105803> <@508125616940515329> <@543900561460822016> <@1011612262743679036> -- I think the implementations finally ended up pretty close, maybe, just maybe, even in consensus. Guys, What is the status of 3860 in the eof tests? 1. Without 3860 2. With 3860 but based on old spec (without https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6249) 3. With updated 3860 (with https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6249) <@425274498732916736> Tests in ethereum/tests, branch 'develop' (default) in EIPTests/stEIP3540 are based on the "new" unified spec and without 3860. Once the 3860 is merged in geth we will probably update the tests. So tests assume shanghaicore + eof but without 3860? Ah okay thanks This is also the question how do we want to continue testing? - Shanghai+EIP3540 - Shanghai+eof1 - Cancun My opinion is shanghai+eof1 it makes sense since we still dont know what goes into cancun <@211091239112671234> <@543900561460822016> can geth support `Shanghai+eof1`? This was about two years ago when I was working on TurboGeth. excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
I uploaded a new version of EOF tests on the execution python test specs here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/pull/23

There are only 4 failing tests for geth at the moment, for which I could not produce test vectors, but in total there were 1886 tests we are now able to produce and package in this file
